items.title: Take a short walk after meals
items.text: Your sugar rose about 19.9 mg/dL less after meals when you walked. Aim for 10 to 20 minutes after dinner, where the program saw the biggest gain (18.3 mg/dL). A check in real adults (CGMacros) pointed the same way, at about a fifth of the program's size, but it is not proven there yet.

rejected.text: Walking after dinner can help with your sugar, which rose about 19.9 mg/dL less after meals when you walked. Try to walk for 10 to 20 minutes after dinner to see the biggest gain, which was 18.3 mg/dL in the program.

items.title: Move dinner earlier
items.text: When you have dinner at 8 pm or later, your sugar rose about 9.2 mg/dL more after late dinners than after earlier ones. Try to start dinner before 8 pm, as sugar rose 13.3 mg/dL more after a dinner at 8-9 pm than after one before 6 pm.

items.title: Aim for a 13-hour overnight break
items.text: Your overnight fast averaged 11.8 hours, and some nights reached 13 hours. In the program, adding an overnight fast to coaching changed HbA1c by -0.03 points compared with coaching alone.
